pezzi.1: How a team of agents is put together: eleven roles with permissions tuned one by one, control over loops that go nowhere, memory that survives a restart.
pezzi.3: How a team of agents is put together: eleven roles with permissions tuned one by one, control over loops that go nowhere, memory that survives a restart.
pezzi.4: Andrea Sforna AI: design, security and maintenance of AI agent systems
pezzi.6: How a team of agents is put together: eleven roles with permissions tuned one by one, control over loops that go nowhere, memory that survives a restart.
pezzi.35: Several agents, separate roles, different permissions
pezzi.36: A single agent that does everything is easy to show off and fragile to keep running. I split the work into roles, and each role holds only the permissions it needs.
pezzi.37: The roles I keep in service
pezzi.38: Ten roles, each with its own tuned permission profile. It is not an org chart: it is a list of the things each one cannot do.
pezzi.42: Takes in the requests and decides who works. It does not execute in place of the others.
pezzi.44: It executes and delegates to no one: the chain stops here.
pezzi.46: It cannot write. It can only read and judge, and it has no stake in declaring the work finished.
pezzi.48: It hands out the work and counts the loops: it warns at the eighth, and it doesn’t go past the sixteenth.
pezzi.50: It works on the project files, with the development tools and nothing more.
pezzi.52: It designs and does not publish.
pezzi.54: It checks that nothing leaves the data behind. It has the power to block, not to send.
pezzi.56: It drives the phone and the devices at home, within a list of tested commands.
pezzi.58: It reads figures and markets, read-only.
pezzi.60: It keeps the thread between sessions. It doesn’t talk to the outside.
pezzi.62: The usual way an agent system breaks is not an error: it is a pair of agents passing the same work back and forth. That is why the loop count sits in the system, not in the instructions.
pezzi.68: A log of who did what
pezzi.70: An agent that starts from scratch every time wastes the time of whoever uses it. I keep a memory that survives a restart, and that ages in a controlled way.
pezzi.72: The decisions taken and the reasons for them
pezzi.73: The stable constraints, distilled from the journals
pezzi.75: Search over the content, computed locally
pezzi.77: The dated notes, which lose weight over time
pezzi.79: Anything with no evidence behind it
pezzi.81: Memory is not declared working: it is measured. I keep a test bench of twenty-four real questions, and I run it again after every change.
pezzi.85: After every change to the system
pezzi.89: The reviewer cannot write. It is a real barrier, not an agreement between gentlemen.
pezzi.91: Splitting work into roles costs steps, time and money. On a simple task it is a waste, and I say so: a deterministic flow or a single agent is enough in most cases.
pezzi.94: Where the permissions live, and why the last layer is not a guarantee.
